The frame continues S5's (map/README.md, Frames): S5's origin, 77 px per metre across the street and in height, 51.25 px of v per metre of depth; only the receding direction drifts (dx_knots, measured here). derivation: Continues S5's frame (map/frames/S5.json F1), so the whole joined world is one coordinate system: the same origin (S5.str.moat_bridge:base.sw, scan 8248, 1565), the same 77 px per metre across the street and in height, and the same 51.25 px of v per metre of depth.

Seam with S5 at u 9400: S5's receding direction there is dx = 32.125 px per metre north (constant east of its bridge knot at u 8250), so this frame's first knot is [9400, 32.125]. A point on the seam then maps to the same metres in both sections.

Knot [10270, 36]: the big hall south of the road, S4.bld.south_hall_10330, whose roof ridge runs straight away from the viewer from its south gable: ridge (10340, 1545) -> (10597, 1210), slope -1.28 (dx 40); the roof's west eave, parallel to it, (9957, 1667) -> (10160, 1340), slope -1.61 (dx 32); the structures agent measured -1.37 and -1.45 on the same lines. Mean slope about -1.42, dx = 51.25 / 1.42 = 36. Both are high lines (eave and ridge, about 4-6 m up), med confidence; nothing at ground level recedes in u 9400-10600 (the houses at the top are frontal, the S5 cart's shaft lies almost level).

Knot [11420, 31.6]: the side edges of the tea-house tables and benches under the eave of S4.bld.south_hall_11450 (props at about 0.6 m): (11330, 1600) -> (11358, 1545), slope -1.96; (11405, 1600) -> (11430, 1560), -1.6; (11493, 1598) -> (11512, 1567), -1.6 (the structures agent: -1.4); mean about -1.65, dx 31.1; and the rounded east end of the courier post's ditch (S4.grd.ditch_11570) (11460, 805) -> (11510, 725), -1.6, dx 32. Short edges, low-med confidence each, but they agree with each other and with S5's bridge (-1.60).

East of u 11420 the knot list stays at 31.6 (constant beyond). Only high or ambiguous edges recede there, and they are shallow: the courier post's west wing eave (11607, 200) -> (11807, 78), -0.61; the open gate leaf's foot (11653, 583) -> (11713, 547), -0.60, which depends on how far the leaf swings; S4.bld.south_hall_12350's ridge (12090, 1395) -> (12600, 1110), -0.56, and its east eave, -0.26; S4.bld.south_pavilion_11760's east hip runs down to the LEFT. Ground-level edges there are steep but humped or curved (the small bridge's west side (11712, 845) -> (11762, 728), -2.34). As in S5 (the tower hall -0.54 over ground -0.88), high lines flatten, so they are not used; this is an open question (questions).
assumptions: East-west and height share S5's scale, 77 px per metre; depth is 51.25 px of v per metre everywhere on the ground (S5's bridge deck). This part's real-size checks say the painter draws far things smaller (questions: the diminution up the silk); the scale is kept unchanged until the lead decides.
Painted figure size is not a scale (S5: street figures about 1.3x life; here 150-195 px on the road, 1.9-2.5 m at 77 px/m). Place by foot point.
Supports other than the ground: the seat on the front of S5's covered ox cart and the temple gate hall's plinth (supports).

questions: Mapped so far: u 9400-12600 (part 1). The rest of S4 (12600-15500) is a later area.

THE DIMINUTION UP THE SILK (reported to the lead before any change): the painter draws far things smaller, so one 77 px/m scale squeezes the top of the silk. Standing adults' painted heights against their foot v: 160-195 px on the road (v 1050-1770), about 150-175 at the courier post and the sedan chairs (v 800-900), 144 (the porter, v 632), 129 (v 474), 94 (the shopkeeper, v 318), 55 (the monk at the temple's side door, v 220): about 0.9 of the road's size at v 850, 0.8 at v 630, 0.5 at v 320 and 0.3 at v 220. Buildings agree: the courier gate's doorway (v 600) is 2.3 x 2.1 m and its eave 2.5 m, the shop house's eave (v 313) 1.4 m, the temple's eave (v 188) 1.5 m and its shut door 0.9 x 0.7 m, the house west of the temple's eave (v 152) 0.7 m. A scale that falls with height on the silk (or a depth rate that grows) would put the top-of-silk buildings further north and make them wider; S5 met the same thing (house_9300's eave 0.7 m, the tower at 0.6 of the street's scale). Until the lead decides, sizes up there are builder choices (map/BUILDING.md rule 5).

THE RECEDING DIRECTION EAST OF u 11420: only high lines recede there and they are shallow (-0.56 to -0.61, dx 84-91); ground evidence west of it is steep (-1.4 to -2.0). The frame keeps 31.6. If the ground really recedes at about -0.6 at the east end, things up the silk there (the courier post's north hall, the fortune-teller's back row) would move about 10 m east.

S4.bld.south_hall_12350's ridge (-0.56) and lower-right eave (-0.26) are not parallel, and its open-front columns stand about 200 px east of its est footprint: a veranda, or a separate hall continuing into part 2. Its footprint is a placeholder.

The courier post's ditch and the small bridge: the planked bank and humped crossing are read as a ditch and a bridge (sections.md: a small bridge in front of the gate); the restyle reads a rail fence and a heap of brushwood. No water is drawn.
The road's south edge between u 9640 and 10160 runs off the silk's bottom edge: the open ground with standing figures continues south beyond the painting there.
